# How to integrate Podio MCP with Hermes

Connect Hermes to Podio MCP. Create tasks from new podio items, find overdue tasks across your podio workspaces, and more using natural language, with authentication handled for you.

![Podio logo](https://logos.composio.dev/api/podio)Podio

Oauth2

Podio is a collaborative work platform for app-based workflows, tasks, items, files, and business data. It gives teams flexible workspaces to organize processes and keep related information together.

143 Tools

## Introduction

Hermes is a 24/7 autonomous agent that lives on your computer or server — it remembers what it learns and evolves as your usage grows.

This guide explains the easiest and most robust way to connect your Podio account to Hermes. You can do this through either **Composio Connect CLI** or **Composio Connect MCP**. For personal use we recommend the CLI, but you won't go wrong with MCP either.

For exact tool slugs and parameter tables, see the [tool catalog in the Composio docs](https://docs.composio.dev/toolkits/podio).

## What is Composio Connect?

Composio Connect is a consumer offering that lets anyone plug 1,700+ applications directly into their agent harness — including Hermes. It can:

- **Search and load tools from relevant toolkits on-demand**, reducing context usage.
- **Chain multiple tools** to accomplish complex workflows via a remote workbench, without excessive back-and-forth with the LLM.
- **Manage app authentication end-to-end** with zero manual overhead.

## Integrating Podio with Hermes

### Using Composio Connect CLI

**1. Install the Composio CLI**

Run the install script directly, or paste `https://composio.dev/hermes` into your Hermes chat box to have it installed for you.

bash

```
curl -fsSL https://composio.dev/install | bash
```

![Hermes authenticating with Composio](https://composio.dev/_next/image?url=%2Ftoolkits%2Fhermes%2Fhermes-authenticate.png&w=1920&q=75)

**2. Authenticate**

Once the CLI is installed, ask Hermes to authenticate with Composio.

**3. Connect to Podio**

Ask your agent to connect to Podio, or simply request any Podio-related task. Hermes will prompt you to authenticate and authorize access.

**4. Done.** You're all set with a new Podio connection.

---

### Using Composio Connect MCP

**1. Get your MCP URL and API Key**

Go to [dashboard.composio.dev](https://dashboard.composio.dev/login?cta_placement=toolkit-framework-hermes-api-key&next=%2F~%2Forg%2Fconnect%2Fclients%2Fhermes) and copy your Connect MCP URL and API key.

![Copy MCP URL and API key from Composio dashboard](https://composio.dev/_next/image?url=%2Ftoolkits%2Fhermes%2Fhermes-mcp-dashboard.png&w=1920&q=75)

**2. Open the Hermes config file**

bash

```
nano ~/.hermes/config.yaml
```

**3. Add the Composio Connect MCP server**

bash

```
mcp_servers:
  composio:
    url: "https://connect.composio.dev/mcp"
    headers:
      x-consumer-api-key: "YOUR_COMPOSIO_API_KEY"
    connect_timeout: 60
    timeout: 180
```

Save with `Ctrl + O`, `Enter`, then exit with `Ctrl + X`.

**4. Restart your Hermes agent**

Once restarted, ask your agent to connect to Podio or request any Podio-related task. It will prompt you to authenticate and authorize access.

**5. Done!**

## What is the Podio MCP server, and what's possible with it?

The Podio MCP server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol that connects your AI agent and assistants like Claude, Cursor, etc directly to your Podio account. It provides structured and secure access to your Podio apps, workspaces, items, tasks, comments, and organization data, so your agent can create and find work items, manage tasks, organize app workflows, and coordinate team activity on your behalf.

- **App and workspace management:** Have your agent find app details, create apps and fields, activate or deactivate apps, and create or archive workspaces.
- **Item and workflow management:** Let the agent create, clone, filter, calculate, export, and delete items across your Podio apps.
- **Task coordination:** Direct your agent to create tasks, assign them to users, add labels and due dates, mark tasks complete, or remove tasks that are no longer needed.
- **Team collaboration:** Instruct your agent to add comments to Podio items and tasks, attach files or links, and remove comments when needed.
- **Organization administration:** Have your agent create organizations, look up administered organizations, manage organization spaces and member roles, and end organization memberships.

## Way Forward

With Podio connected, Hermes can now act on your behalf whenever it detects a relevant task or you ask it to.

From here, you can extend Hermes further:

- **Connect more apps:** Calendar, Slack, Notion, Linear, and hundreds of others are available through the same Composio Connect setup. Each new integration compounds what Hermes can do for you.
- **Build workflows across tools:** Once multiple apps are connected, Hermes can chain actions together — turn an email into a calendar invite, a Slack message into a Linear ticket, or a meeting note into a follow-up draft.
- **Let it learn your patterns:** The more you use Hermes, the better it gets at anticipating how you'd handle recurring tasks. Give it feedback on drafts and decisions, and it will adapt.

If you run into trouble or want to share what you've built, join the [community](https://discord.com/invite/composio) or check out the [Docs](https://docs.composio.dev?cta_placement=toolkit-framework-hermes-docs) for deeper configuration options.

## Frequently asked questions

###

With a standalone Podio MCP server, the agents and LLMs can only access a fixed set of Podio tools tied to that server. However, with the Composio Tool Router, agents can dynamically load tools from Podio and many other apps based on the task at hand, all through a single MCP endpoint.

###

Yes, you can. Hermes fully supports MCP integration. You get structured tool calling, message history handling, and model orchestration while Tool Router takes care of discovering and serving the right Podio tools.

###

Yes, absolutely. You can configure which Podio scopes and actions are allowed when connecting your account to Composio. You can also bring your own OAuth credentials or API configuration so you keep full control over what the agent can do.

###

All sensitive data such as tokens, keys, and configuration is fully encrypted at rest and in transit. Composio is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and follows strict security practices so your Podio data and credentials are handled as safely as possible.
